questions.title: Trace the execution
questions.prompt:
**Tracing** means logging values as code runs. Add one `console.log()` statement **inside** the loop of the starter code so that each pass logs the index and the running total in this exact format:

```

i=1 total=12
i=2 total=27
```

Don't change anything else.

questions.title: Plan the test runs
questions.prompt:
Write a function `isValidPercent(value)` that returns `true` for numbers from 0 to 100 (inclusive) and `false` for anything else, including non-numbers.

Then plan your tests the way the chapter recommends — include the **boundaries** and invalid data. Create an array `testCases` of objects like `{ input: 0, expected: true }` with at least six cases, including `0`, `100`, `-1`, `101` and a string such as `"abc"`. Finally, loop through `testCases` and log `PASS` or `FAIL` for each.
hints: typeof value === "number" checks for a number.
for (const test of testCases) { console.log(isValidPercent(test.input) === test.expected ? "PASS" : "FAIL"); }

tests.name: testCases covers 0, 100, -1, 101 and a string
tests.code:
const inputs = testCases.map(t => t.input);
return testCases.length >= 6 && [0, 100, -1, 101].every(v => inputs.includes(v)) && inputs.some(v => typeof v === "string");

questions.title: Two bugs in the cart
questions.prompt:
`cartTotal(items)` should return the total price of all items (price × quantity), with 10% off when the total is **over 100**. It has **two bugs**. Use tracing to find them and fix them.

```
cartTotal([{ price: 20, qty: 2 }, { price: 15, qty: 1 }])    // 55
cartTotal([{ price: 60, qty: 2 }])                            // 108
```
hints: Is total being added to, or replaced, on each pass?

tests.name: First example returns 55
tests.code: return cartTotal([{ price: 20, qty: 2 }, { price: 15, qty: 1 }]) === 55;
